# Basic Portuguese — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/portuguese-basics.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/portuguese-basics.ttl`](../decks/portuguese-basics.ttl) · **Cards:** 120 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

120 basic Portuguese words and phrases for beginners: the numbers 0–20, the tens and 100, the days of the week, the months, eight colours, family members, greetings and polite phrases, everyday nouns, six adjectives and 16 verbs, in European Portuguese spelt by the 1990 Orthographic Agreement, with Brazilian forms in notes where they differ. The front shows the Portuguese word, nouns with their article (o livro, a casa); the back gives its English and Swedish meaning, or the digits for a number. Words from Wikidata's lexemes and the US Foreign Service Institute's Portuguese course (public domain), checked against Priberam, Wiktionary and Folkets lexikon.

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose terms allow any reuse: Wikidata's lexemes and items (CC0 1.0: Portuguese lemmas, genders, forms, glosses and Portuguese, English and Swedish labels) and the Foreign Service Institute's Portuguese Programmatic Course, Volume 1 (1974), a work of the United States Government with no copyright protection under 17 U.S.C. § 105 (eight phrases with their meaning, and a check of sim, não and oi). The selection of words is the authors' own. The English and Swedish renderings not taken from Wikidata or the FSI course are the usual equivalents chosen by the authors; several are the same short stock glosses that English Wiktionary or Folkets lexikon give, as their source records say. Single words and fixed greetings such as "nice to meet you" or "ingen orsak" are facts of usage, not protectable expression, so this does not carry those sources' licences into the deck; no definition, example, comment or list was taken from them. The rule applied throughout: English and Swedish equivalents and the facts in the notes not given by a content source are the authors' own knowledge, worded by them and only confirmed in a verification source. Priberam's dictionary (all rights reserved; its terms forbid reproducing any part of the website and deep linking to it), the Vocabulário Ortográfico Comum (its publisher, the IILP, reserves all rights), Portuguese and English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Folkets lexikon (CC BY-SA 2.5) were used for verification only. So no source requires attribution or share-alike for the deck, although all are credited in its provenance. The quotations in this provenance report are not covered by the deck's CC0 dedication or the repository's MIT licence: quotations from Priberam (© Priberam Informática, S.A., all rights reserved) are cut to grammatical labels and the first few words of a definition, the least that identifies the entry checked, and its entries are named by headword, not linked; quotations from the VOC (© IILP, all rights reserved) are its spelling and word-class labels; quotations from Portuguese and English Wiktionary are © Wiktionary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0; quotations from Folkets lexikon are CC BY-SA 2.5; quotations from the FSI course are in the public domain; Wikidata data is CC0.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Variety and spelling. The deck follows European Portuguese (the norm of Portugal), spelt by the 1990 Orthographic Agreement as Portugal applies it, and prefers words common to Portugal and Brazil. Where the two differ for a card, the Brazilian form is named in a note (dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove; o cachorro; oi). European Portuguese was chosen because Wikidata's Portuguese lexemes for the numbers from 11 up are European (for example L1635008 dezesseis is glossed "o mesmo que dezasseis") and because the deck uses the Portuguese national orthographic vocabulary (VOP) and Priberam's European-norm view to check spelling. Words whose everyday form differs (o comboio and o trem, o pequeno-almoço and o café da manhã, castanho and marrom) were left out rather than given two answers.
3. Word list. A candidate list for a first Portuguese course was drawn up by hand from the brief's categories (numbers 0–20, the tens and 100; days; months; colours; family; greetings and polite phrases; everyday nouns; adjectives; verbs), choosing the most basic word for each concept and following the authored French and Spanish decks where the languages allow. No frequency list or textbook word list was copied.
4. Wikidata lexemes. SPARQL query 1 fetched every Portuguese lexeme (language Q5146) whose lemma is a candidate, with its category, gender (P5185), senses, English and Portuguese glosses and sense items (P5137); the list included the Brazilian variants and alternatives (quatorze, dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove, cinza, cachorro, oi, tchau, obrigada) and nine phrases. irmã, filha and all phrases were not found as lemmas. The lexeme search (calls 2) found irmã and filha as forms of irmão (L447160) and filho (L677502), the greetings only as hyphenated nouns (bom-dia L1640417, boa-tarde L1646749, boa-noite L1626801), desculpar (L1665828) for desculpe, and nothing for até logo, até amanhã, com licença, por favor, de nada, obrigada, tchau or oi. The obrigado lexemes found have no interjection sense: the adjective L1608351 means obliged or grateful, and the noun L1664143 is a thank-you as a noun ("agradecimento que se dá a alguém"); the noun is cited as supporting evidence on the obrigado card. The full JSON of every lexeme found was fetched with API calls 3; for each card the lexeme of the right category was used (the numeral lexeme for 1–10, the noun lexeme for 0 and 11–100, the adjective lexeme for colours and adjectives, and so on).
5. Wikidata items. The items of the chosen senses, the number, day, month, colour and family items, the items found with the item search (calls 6: hello Q12068060, good afternoon Q19279334, good evening Q19279366, goodbye Q2506912, purple Q3257809), and thank you Q19279214, yes Q6452715 and no Q1814990, which the item search did not return among its first results and were taken from the records of the authored French deck (the number, day, month, colour and family items are also the ones that deck uses) were fetched with API calls 5 (labels and aliases in pt, pt-br, en, sv and mul). Where a sense's item is broader than the card, the narrower item was used for labels: irmão and irmã (sense item Q31184, sibling) use brother Q10861465 and sister Q595094; filho and filha (Q29514218, child) use son Q177232 and daughter Q308194; água (Q29053744, liquid water) uses water Q283.
6. Phrases from the FSI course. For the phrases with no usable lexeme, the Internet Archive was searched for public-domain Foreign Service Institute Portuguese courses (call 8). The Portuguese Programmatic Course, Volume 1 (1974, in the ERIC archive) was the only FSI student text found; its OCR text was downloaded and saved as <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt (call 9) and searched with grep (call 10), and each hit was read in context with the English column (lines and page markers are given in the evidence). bom dia, boa tarde and boa noite (Unit 15), obrigado (Unit 6), por favor (Unit 11), desculpe and de nada (Unit 16), muito prazer (Unit 9), sim (Unit 10) and não (Unit 20) were found. até logo, até amanhã and com licença were not found in the OCR text and are not cards. The course teaches Brazilian Portuguese. Each phrase used except muito prazer has an entry in Priberam's European-norm view (bom-dia, boa-tarde, boa-noite, obrigado, and por favor, de nada under favor and nada; desculpe under desculpar). muito prazer has no entry in Priberam or Portuguese Wiktionary; Priberam's page says only that its checker FLiP recognises it, and Portuguese Wiktionary gives prazer as an interjection said on being introduced, with a pronunciation for Portugal. The English backs follow the course's glosses where they match (good morning, good afternoon, good evening and good night, please, excuse me); "thank you" is the Wikidata label of Q19279214, and "you’re welcome", "nice to meet you" and "sorry" are the authors' usual renderings.
7. Writing the cards. The front is the Portuguese word as in the lexeme's lemma (or the FSI phrase), lower case. Nouns are preceded by the definite article that shows their gender (o livro, a casa). Days and months are given without an article, with their gender in a note; colours and adjectives in the masculine singular with the feminine in a note; verbs in the infinitive. The back is the authors' own short English and Swedish rendering of the main sense: for nouns the bare noun, for verbs the infinitive (English "to …", Swedish "att …"), for numbers the digits (tagged zxx, as digits are in no language). English and Swedish follow the Wikidata labels where an item has them; otherwise they are the usual equivalents, chosen by the authors and checked in English Wiktionary and Folkets lexikon. Where a word has two everyday English or Swedish equivalents both are given (cidade: city, town; grande: big, large; falar: tala, prata; ir: gå, åka). English and Swedish equivalents and the facts in the notes not given by a content source are the authors' own knowledge of the languages, worded by the authors and only confirmed in the verification sources.
8. Notes. A short note was added where it helps a beginner and a source confirms it: the gender of each day (with the short forms segunda, terça, quarta, quinta and sexta) and month, months in lower case since the 1990 Agreement, the feminine of each colour and adjective, um and dois with their feminines (and um as the article), the Brazilian spellings of 16, 17 and 19, quatorze, cem and cento, os pais and os irmãos, avô and avó, oi, tchau, obrigada, the times of day for the greetings, de nada as the reply to thanks, the literal meaning of muito prazer, não as "not", cão and cachorro, mulher as wife, a amiga, a mão and o dia, noite as the evening, novo as young, ser and estar, and the Swedish gå/åka and tack. The example phrases in the notes (um livro, não sei, sou sueco, estou em casa, estou cansado, ele é muito novo, en kaffe, tack) are the authors' own.
9. Cross-checking. Every single-word headword was looked up in the Vocabulário Ortográfico Comum, Portuguese version (calls 13; spelling and word class or gender), in Priberam's dictionary (calls 14; European-norm reading, part of speech, gender and first definition), in Portuguese Wiktionary (calls 15; part of speech, gender template, first definition and inflection table) and in the Portuguese section of English Wiktionary (calls 16; English meaning). The phrases were looked up in Priberam, Portuguese Wiktionary and English Wiktionary (the VOC records single words, not phrases); muito prazer has an entry in none of the first two, so its parts were checked (prazer). The usage notes on cem and cento were checked in English Wiktionary's wikitext of both words (calls 17). Every Swedish back was checked in Folkets lexikon (calls 18). Python scripts built the evidence lines from the responses saved on 4 October 2026, so each quotation is what the source returned, with wiki markup and HTML removed; Priberam's page text was reduced to its European-norm reading (spans marked as Brazilian removed). Because Priberam's terms forbid reproducing any part of its website, its quotations were then cut (quality-control round 3) to the part of speech, gender, usage and norm labels and the first seven words or so of the definition, with "…" where cut and "[…]" for left-out parentheses, and its entries are named by headword rather than linked; other quotations are cut at about 160 characters and marked with "…". OCR quotations from the FSI course are given with the intended letters and the OCR reading in brackets.
10. Machine checks. The dossier's Wikidata checks (the Portuguese, English and Swedish label or alias of each linked item that matches the card's text, and the mul digit label of each number) are re-run against live Wikidata by the builder on every build. Wikidata lexemes cannot be checked by the builder (it checks items only); the lexeme facts in the evidence were read from the API responses of 4 October 2026. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
11. Excluded: até logo, até amanhã and com licença (no lexeme and not in the public-domain FSI text), tchau and oi as cards of their own (informal alternatives, named in notes), words whose everyday form differs between Portugal and Brazil (o comboio/o trem, o autocarro/o ônibus, o pequeno-almoço/o café da manhã, a rapariga/a garota, castanho/marrom, cor-de-rosa/rosa, cor de laranja/laranja), the pronouns tu and você (whose use differs between the two varieties), and words with two equally common meanings that a single card cannot separate (o tempo: time or weather).

## Selection

120 cards: the cardinal numbers 0–20, the tens 30–90 and 100 (29); the seven days of the week; the twelve months; eight colours (vermelho, azul, verde, amarelo, preto, branco, cinzento, roxo); eight family members (mãe, pai, irmão, irmã, filho, filha, avô, avó); twelve greetings and polite phrases (olá, bom dia, boa tarde, boa noite, adeus, obrigado, por favor, de nada, desculpe, muito prazer, sim, não); 22 everyday nouns (house, water, bread, milk, apple, book, table, chair, door, window, dog, cat, city, street, school, man, woman, friend, hand, day, night, week); six common adjectives (grande, pequeno, bom, mau, novo, velho); and 16 common verbs in the infinitive (ser, estar, ter, ir, fazer, vir, falar, comer, beber, querer, poder, ver, ler, escrever, dormir, trabalhar). The list was chosen by the deck's authors for a first course, not copied from any frequency list or textbook. The deck follows European Portuguese, spelt by the 1990 Orthographic Agreement; words common to Portugal and Brazil were preferred, and where a card's word differs in Brazil the Brazilian form is in a note (dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove, o cachorro, oi). Nouns are given with the definite article (o, a); colours and adjectives in the masculine singular with the feminine in a note; days and months without an article and in lower case, with their gender in a note. Left out: até logo, até amanhã and com licença (no open content source gives them), tchau and oi as separate cards, words whose everyday form differs between Portugal and Brazil (train, bus, breakfast, girl, brown, pink, orange), the pronouns tu and você, and words with two equally common meanings (o tempo).

## Queries

**1. Portuguese lexemes (Q5146) for every candidate lemma, with lexical category, grammatical gender (P5185), senses, English and Portuguese glosses and the item for each sense (P5137). POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql** (Wikidata (Portuguese lexemes and items))

```
SELECT ?lexeme ?lemma ?category ?gender ?sense ?glossEn ?glossPt ?item WHERE {
  VALUES ?lemma { "zero"@pt "um"@pt "dois"@pt "três"@pt "quatro"@pt "cinco"@pt "seis"@pt "sete"@pt "oito"@pt "nove"@pt "dez"@pt "onze"@pt "doze"@pt "treze"@pt "catorze"@pt "quatorze"@pt "quinze"@pt "dezasseis"@pt "dezesseis"@pt "dezassete"@pt "dezessete"@pt "dezoito"@pt "dezanove"@pt "dezenove"@pt "vinte"@pt "trinta"@pt "quarenta"@pt "cinquenta"@pt "sessenta"@pt "setenta"@pt "oitenta"@pt "noventa"@pt "cem"@pt "segunda-feira"@pt "terça-feira"@pt "quarta-feira"@pt "quinta-feira"@pt "sexta-feira"@pt "sábado"@pt "domingo"@pt "janeiro"@pt "fevereiro"@pt "março"@pt "abril"@pt "maio"@pt "junho"@pt "julho"@pt "agosto"@pt "setembro"@pt "outubro"@pt "novembro"@pt "dezembro"@pt "vermelho"@pt "azul"@pt "verde"@pt "amarelo"@pt "preto"@pt "branco"@pt "cinzento"@pt "cinza"@pt "roxo"@pt "laranja"@pt "mãe"@pt "pai"@pt "irmão"@pt "irmã"@pt "filho"@pt "filha"@pt "avô"@pt "avó"@pt "olá"@pt "oi"@pt "adeus"@pt "tchau"@pt "obrigado"@pt "obrigada"@pt "sim"@pt "não"@pt "desculpe"@pt "casa"@pt "água"@pt "pão"@pt "leite"@pt "maçã"@pt "livro"@pt "mesa"@pt "cadeira"@pt "porta"@pt "janela"@pt "cão"@pt "cachorro"@pt "gato"@pt "cidade"@pt "rua"@pt "escola"@pt "homem"@pt "mulher"@pt "amigo"@pt "mão"@pt "dia"@pt "noite"@pt "semana"@pt "ano"@pt "dinheiro"@pt "carro"@pt "grande"@pt "pequeno"@pt "bom"@pt "mau"@pt "novo"@pt "velho"@pt "ser"@pt "estar"@pt "ter"@pt "ir"@pt "fazer"@pt "vir"@pt "falar"@pt "comer"@pt "beber"@pt "querer"@pt "poder"@pt "ver"@pt "ler"@pt "escrever"@pt "dormir"@pt "trabalhar"@pt "comprar"@pt "morar"@pt "viver"@pt "bom dia"@pt "boa tarde"@pt "boa noite"@pt "até logo"@pt "até amanhã"@pt "por favor"@pt "de nada"@pt "com licença"@pt "muito obrigado"@pt }
  ?lexeme dct:language wd:Q5146 ;
          wikibase:lemma ?lemma ;
          wikibase:lexicalCategory ?category .
  OPTIONAL { ?lexeme wdt:P5185 ?gender . }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?lexeme ontolex:sense ?sense .
    OPTIONAL { ?sense skos:definition ?glossEn . FILTER(LANG(?glossEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?sense skos:definition ?glossPt . FILTER(LANG(?glossPt) = "pt") }
    OPTIONAL { ?sense wdt:P5137 ?item . }
  }
}
ORDER BY ?lemma ?lexeme ?sense
```

**10. Phrase look-ups in the OCR text; the hits were then read in context by line number, and a Python script (<scratch>/fsipages.py, given after the grep commands) printed each line with the nearest page markers before and after it (lines matching ^\s*\d{1,2}\.\d{1,2}\s*$)** (Portuguese [Brazilian] Programmatic Course, Volume 1 (Foreign Service Institute, 1974), as scanned in the ERIC archive on the Internet Archive (ERIC ED096854))

```
grep -n -i -E "obrigad|bom dia|boa tarde|boa noite|at[eé] logo|at[eé] amanh|por favor|de nada|desculp|com licen|copyright|public domain|For sale" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -E "bo[mn]\s+dia|boa\s+tarde|boa\s+noite|at.\s+logo|at.\s+amanh|por\s+favor|de\s+nada|com\s+licen|good\s+morning|good\s+afternoon|good\s+evening|good\s+night|you.re\s+welcome|see\s+you|excuse\s+me|please|good-?by" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -E "at.\s+(logo|amanh|breve|ja)|licen.a|tchau|adeus|^\s*sim\b|\bsim[ ,.]+\s+(yes|n)|ol.\b" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -E "lic[eo]n|tudo\s+bem|como\s+vai|prazer|at[eé3]\s+j[aá]|at[eé3]\s+a\s+" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -E "obrigad|n.o,\s+obrig" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -E "dean|director|school of language|copyright|reproduc" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -E "^\s*(UNIT|Unit)\s+[0-9IlO]+\s*$" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
grep -n -i -w -E "ol[aá6]" <scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt
python3 <scratch>/fsipages.py 7084 13225 14916 16645 16650 24016 24036 24048 24472 26647 26650 26657 26660 26673 34200 34212 34420 34422 35738
# <scratch>/fsipages.py:
L = open("<scratch>/fsi-vol1.txt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().split("\n")
pat = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d{1,2})\.(\d{1,2})\s*$")
for n in map(int, sys.argv[1:]):
    prev = next((f"{L[i].strip()} (line {i+1})" for i in range(n - 1, 0, -1) if pat.match(L[i])), None)
    nxt = next((f"{L[i].strip()} (line {i+1})" for i in range(n, len(L)) if pat.match(L[i])), None)
    print(n, repr(L[n - 1].strip()), "| prev marker", prev, "| next marker", nxt)
```

**14. Priberam's European-norm entry per headword (and dezesseis, dezessete, dezenove, cinza, cachorro, tchau, oi, obrigada, quatorze, cento, segunda, terça, quarta, quinta, sexta, pais, desculpar and desculpa), fetched two seconds apart and saved one file per headword. Each page was reduced with BeautifulSoup (<scratch>/pribclean.py, run with uv run --with beautifulsoup4): keep the text of div#resultados, remove <script> and <style>, remove the spans of class varpb (Brazilian norm), replace each <aAO> element (pre-1990-Agreement spelling) by "[aAO: …]", collapse white space and drop the site's "Sabia que? …" hint. In quality-control round 3 the quotations were cut to labels and the first words of a definition, and muito prazer and prazer were looked up. Since quality-control round 4 the request URLs are recorded as one URL pattern and the list of headwords, not as one link per entry, because Priberam's terms forbid deep linking** (Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (online), European-norm view)

```
URL pattern: https://dicionario.priberam.org/pt-pt/<headword> (headword URL-encoded, e.g. três as tr%C3%AAs, muito prazer as muito%20prazer), one request per headword below.
Headwords, in order of fetching: zero; um; dois; três; quatro; cinco; seis; sete; oito; nove; dez; onze; doze; treze; catorze; quinze; dezasseis; dezassete; dezoito; dezanove; vinte; trinta; quarenta; cinquenta; sessenta; setenta; oitenta; noventa; cem; segunda-feira; terça-feira; quarta-feira; quinta-feira; sexta-feira; sábado; domingo; janeiro; fevereiro; março; abril; maio; junho; julho; agosto; setembro; outubro; novembro; dezembro; vermelho; azul; verde; amarelo; preto; branco; cinzento; roxo; mãe; pai; irmão; irmã; filho; filha; avô; avó; olá; bom dia; boa tarde; boa noite; adeus; obrigado; por favor; de nada; desculpe; muito prazer; sim; não; casa; água; pão; leite; maçã; livro; mesa; cadeira; porta; janela; cão; gato; cidade; rua; escola; homem; mulher; amigo; mão; dia; noite; semana; grande; pequeno; bom; mau; novo; velho; ser; estar; ter; ir; fazer; vir; falar; comer; beber; querer; poder; ver; ler; escrever; dormir; trabalhar; dezesseis; dezessete; dezenove; cinza; cachorro; tchau; oi; obrigada; quatorze; cento; segunda; terça; quarta; quinta; sexta; pais; desculpar; desculpa; prazer (round 1); muito prazer (round 1)
```

**18. Folkets lexikon, both directions, and its about page (licence); entries looked up by headword and idiom; the matching code and follow-up searches are given after the URLs** (Folkets lexikon (English–Swedish and Swedish–English))

```
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_en_sv_public.xml
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_sv_en_public.xml
https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/om.html
# index and matching (Python, <scratch>/folkets.py):
for w in ET.parse(fn).getroot().iter("word"):
    head = w.get("value").replace("|", "")
    tr = [t.get("value") for t in w.findall("translation")]
    idx.setdefault(head.lower(), []).append(("word", head, w.get("class"), tr))
    for idm in w.findall("idiom"):
        itr = [t.get("value") for t in idm.findall("translation")]
        idx.setdefault(idm.get("value").lower().rstrip("!.?"), []).append(("idiom", idm.get("value"), head, itr))
# each Swedish part of the back (split at commas and " eller ", "att " removed) must be a translation of an English part in the en-sv index,
# or have an English part among its translations in the sv-en index; the eight backs that did not match automatically were looked up by hand:
lookups: sv lila, hej då, tack, ingen orsak, ursäkta, förlåt, trevligt att träffas, åka, kunna; en purple, goodbye, thank you, thanks, you're welcome, excuse me, sorry, nice to meet you, pleased to meet you, can, be able to, go, please, grandfather, grandmother
grep -n -i -E 'value="(hej ?då|hejdå|adjö|bye)"' <scratch>/folkets_sv_en_public.xml <scratch>/folkets_en_sv_public.xml
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 32 findings: 18 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 12 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (256 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 120 cards: every Portuguese form, gender, English and Swedish meaning and note against the content sources and the verification sources; the builder's Wikidata checks.

Every card has evidence from a content source (Wikidata, or the FSI course for eight phrases) and at least two verification sources. The VOC (Portuguese version) and Priberam's European-norm entries agree with the spelling of every single-word headword; the gender shown on every noun, day and month card agrees with the Wikidata lexeme (its gender statement, or for irmão, irmã, filho, filha, gato and amigo the gender of its forms), the VOC and Priberam. English Wiktionary confirms every English back except two parts: "sorry" on desculpe (Wiktionary glosses desculpar as "to forgive" and "to apologise"; FSI gives "excuse me") and "little" on pequeno (Wiktionary: "small"; Wikidata's item small, Q16042592, has the alias "little"). Folkets lexikon or a Swedish Wikidata label confirms every Swedish back. The builder's Wikidata checks cover the Portuguese, English and Swedish labels or aliases of 99 linked items (256 checks), including the digit label of every number; they all pass. Discrepancies between sources and how they were resolved are listed below. No independent review round has been run yet.

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent final reviewer · **Scope:** All 120 cards against the reviewer's own knowledge and the dossier's evidence; the description and its counts, keywords, study direction, language tags, and the three fixes logged in round 4.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| por-favor | The Swedish back "snälla" on its own can sound pleading or childlike; polite Swedish requests normally use "tack" or "var snäll och …". Suggested changing the back to "snälla, tack" or "var snäll och", or keeping it with the existing backNote. | Declined. "snälla" is the one-word Swedish equivalent of the request word please and is listed for it in Folkets lexikon (query 18), already cited on the card; "var snäll och" is a phrase that needs a verb after it and "snälla, tack" is not idiomatic. The card's backNote already tells the learner that Swedish requests usually end with tack (en kaffe, tack), which covers the register point, as the reviewer's own option allows. | rejected |
